# Dhātusosaṁsandana Sutta (Iti 78 (It 3.29 PTS It 69))

**ID:** Iti 78 (It 3.29 PTS It 69)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Dhātusosaṁsandana Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Converging Elements
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti78
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhātusosaṁsandana Sutta* ("Converging Elements") is the twenty-ninth discourse in the section of Threes (Tikanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka*, cataloged as Iti 78 (PTS It 69) [SuttaCentral; Lim Hwee San 2009]. The sutta expounds the principle that beings converge and associate according to their properties or elements (*dhātu*): beings of low dispositions (*hīnādhimuttikā*) associate with those of low disposition, while those bent on the lovely (*kalyāṇādhimuttikā*) come together with like-minded companions [SuttaCentral; Lim Hwee San 2009]. This observation is affirmed to hold universally in the past, future, and present [Lim Hwee San 2009].

A full Chinese parallel exists at T 765.113 (*Tong jie* 同界) [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, closely related material occurs in the *Dhātu Saṁyutta* (SN 14), including the *Hīnādhimuttika Sutta*, *Caṅkama Sutta* (SN 14.15), and *Sagāthā Sutta* (SN 14.16), with further verse parallels found in the *Theragāthā* (*Somamittattheragāthā*, Thag 2.14; *Vimalattheragāthā*, Thag 3.16) and the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (SA 446 and SA 448) [SuttaCentral; Lim Hwee San 2009]. Text-reuse analyses from DharmaNexus corroborate these connections, showing extensive reuse with the *Dhātu Saṁyutta* (76 matches; especially §2.1–5.4 with SN 14.1.2–14.4.4), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* (Vb 16), and verse alignments with *Somamittattheragāthā* (§6.2–8.4 with Thag 2.14 §0.4–2.5) and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as alignments with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 101) [DharmaNexus]. The sutta is also referenced in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.7.4) [SuttaCentral].
